newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo plans Seretide filings in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo plans Seretide filings in 1998.

text.p: Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Friday it planned to seek regulatory approval for a new combination asthma drug, Seretide, in 1998.
In its research and development update, Glaxo said Seretide was a combination of its long-acting bronchodilator Serevent and the inhaled steroid Flixotide/Flovent.
"Initial trials indicate that its effect is greater than the addition of the benefits from using the two products separately," the group said.

Glaxo also announced that its metered dose inhaler for asthma, the Flovent diskhaler, had won approvable status from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and that it was about to launch its first non-CFC metered dose inhalers in Germany.
Glaxo Wellcome is the world's leading respiratory company in terms of sales, with market share of more than twice its nearest competitor.

"Prospects for future growth are underscored by the fact that asthma is currently under-treated, with less than half the sufferers in the western world receiving medicines," scientist Rick Fuller told analysts.
"Changing approaches to the treatment of asthma mean that significant opportunities for growth lie in countries such as the U.S. and Japan," he added.

Also in the respiratory area, Fuller highlighted the company's influenza treatment Zanamivir, which has recently entered late-stage trials. The company plans to seek regulatory approval for the drug next year.
He said the drug offered the potential to alleviate the impact of flu on people particularly at risk, and noted that 10,000 people died from the disease every year in the U.S.
